questions.stem: A seller agrees to sell her house to a buyer for $250,000, well below its $320,000 market value. Later she claims the contract is invalid because the price was too low. Which is most accurate?
choices: The contract is void because the consideration must equal the market value
The contract is voidable by the seller because she received less than fair value
The contract is valid; courts generally don't weigh whether the price was fair
The contract is unenforceable unless an appraisal supports the agreed price
questions.explanation: A contract needs good and valuable consideration from both sides, and courts generally don't judge its adequacy. A low price agreed to by competent parties doesn't make the contract void or voidable.

questions.stem: A buyer and seller sign a written purchase contract that spells out the price, closing date and inclusions. Classified by how it was formed, this contract is
choices: express
implied
unilateral
executed
questions.explanation: An express contract states its terms in words, oral or written. An implied contract arises from conduct; unilateral and executed describe who is bound and stage of performance, not how the contract was formed.

questions.stem: Which statement by a listing broker is most likely puffing rather than a statement of fact a buyer could rely on?
choices: "The furnace was replaced with a new unit just last year."
"This kitchen has the best view in the whole neighborhood."
"The roof on the house is only two years old."
"The basement has never had any water in it."
questions.explanation: Puffing is a vague opinion or exaggeration a reasonable buyer wouldn't rely on as fact. The other statements are specific facts; if false, they would be misrepresentations.

questions.stem: An owner deployed overseas wants her brother to sign the deed conveying her house while she is away. What does the brother need?
choices: A power of attorney from the owner authorizing him to convey the property
A letter from the listing broker confirming that the owner agreed to the sale
Nothing more, because a close family member may sign for an absent owner
A court order declaring the owner legally incompetent to sign contracts
questions.explanation: Someone signing for another person needs proper authority, typically a power of attorney, which is usually recorded when used to convey real property. Being a relative gives no authority to sign.

questions.stem: While reviewing a purchase contract, a seller asks his broker whether a clause would hold up in court and what his legal rights would be if the buyer backed out. What should the broker do?
choices: Explain the seller's legal rights based on the broker's own experience
Rewrite the clause in plain language so that it is clearly enforceable
Tell the seller the clause is standard language that needs no review
Recommend that the seller consult an attorney
questions.explanation: Brokers fill in forms but may not give legal advice or draft original contract language. Questions about legal rights or enforceability should go to an attorney.

questions.stem: A buyer makes an offer on a home. Before the seller responds, the buyer dies. The seller then signs the offer. Which is true?
choices: A contract was formed that is binding on the buyer's estate
The offer ended at the buyer's death, so no contract was formed
The contract is voidable at the option of the buyer's heirs
The seller may choose to enforce the contract against the estate
questions.explanation: An offer terminates if either party dies or becomes incompetent before acceptance. Because the offer no longer existed, the seller's signature couldn't create a contract.

questions.stem: A seller is already under contract with one buyer when a second buyer submits a written offer before closing. What should the listing broker do?
choices: Reject it on the seller's behalf because the home is under contract
Hold it until the first contract either closes or falls through
Present it to the seller promptly; the seller may accept it as a backup
Share its terms with the first buyer so that buyer can match it
questions.explanation: Listing brokers must present all written offers promptly, even when the property is already under contract (in Colorado, C.R.S. 12-10-404 requires this), so the seller can decide whether to accept one as a backup, which is subject to the first contract failing. Holding or rejecting it takes the decision away from the seller, and sharing one buyer's terms with another requires the seller's permission.

questions.stem: A seller hired a particular broker because of his marketing skill. The broker wants to transfer the listing agreement to an unrelated broker. Generally, the listing
choices: can't be assigned without the seller's consent, because it is a personal services contract
can be freely assigned, because most contracts are assignable unless they say otherwise
becomes void the moment the broker attempts to assign it without asking
can be assigned only if the new broker pays the seller separate consideration
questions.explanation: Most contracts are assignable, but contracts that depend on a person's skill, such as a listing agreement, generally can't be assigned without the other party's consent.

questions.stem: A purchase contract makes the buyer's obligation to close depend on the buyer obtaining loan approval by a stated date. This provision is a(n)
choices: right of first refusal
option
amendment
contingency
questions.explanation: A contingency is a condition that must be met before a party is obligated to perform. If it fails, the protected party can usually terminate without default by giving notice by the deadline.

questions.stem: A buyer backs out without legal excuse. The contract lets the seller either keep the earnest money or pursue actual damages. The seller resells to another buyer for $20,000 less and sues the first buyer for that loss. The seller is seeking
choices: specific performance
rescission
liquidated damages
compensatory damages
questions.explanation: Compensatory damages are money to cover the actual loss caused by the breach. Liquidated damages would be the amount agreed in advance, such as the earnest money.

questions.stem: A buyer signs a purchase contract that calls for no earnest money deposit. Which is correct?
choices: It can be valid, because the buyer's promise to pay is consideration
It is void, because every purchase contract requires earnest money
It becomes valid only after the buyer deposits money with a broker
It is valid, but the seller has no remedy if the buyer later defaults
questions.explanation: Earnest money isn't required for a valid contract; the buyer's promise to pay supplies consideration. The seller can still pursue remedies such as damages if the buyer defaults.

questions.stem: A seller breached a purchase contract, but the buyer waited many years to sue, past the deadline state law sets for that kind of claim. The buyer's claim is most likely
choices: still enforceable, because the seller never cured the breach
void from the start, because the seller breached the contract
unenforceable, because the statute of limitations has run
limited to specific performance instead of money damages
questions.explanation: A statute of limitations sets a deadline for filing suit. Once it runs, the claim can no longer be enforced in court.

questions.stem: A homeowner hires a well-known artist to paint a mural in her living room, and the artist dies before starting. The contract is most likely discharged by
choices: novation
mutual release
impossibility
substantial performance
questions.explanation: Impossibility discharges a contract when performance can't be done, such as when a party to a personal-services contract dies. Novation and mutual release require agreement of the parties.

questions.stem: After a purchase contract is signed but before closing, the buyer holds
choices: legal title, while the seller keeps equitable title
a leasehold estate until the closing takes place
no interest in the property until the deed is recorded
equitable title, while the seller still holds legal title
questions.explanation: A signed purchase contract gives the buyer equitable title, an interest in the property, even though the seller keeps legal title until closing.

questions.stem: A lease runs from January 1 through June 30 of the same year. Which is true about ending it?
choices: It ends automatically on June 30 without notice
It is a periodic tenancy that requires notice set by state law
It continues month-to-month until the landlord gives notice
It is a tenancy at will that ends only when either party dies
questions.explanation: A lease with a definite start and end date is an estate for years, whatever its length, and it ends automatically. A periodic tenancy renews itself and requires notice to end.

questions.stem: Which is most likely a material fact that a broker who knows of it should disclose to a buyer?
choices: The listing broker thinks the backyard is the nicest on the block
The state has approved a highway next to the property
The seller will move her furniture out before the closing date
The home's exterior was painted a different color five years ago
questions.explanation: A material fact is one that would affect a reasonable buyer's decision or the price paid; a planned highway next door qualifies. The others are opinions or facts that don't affect value or desirability.

questions.stem: A seller gives the buyer a completed seller's property disclosure statement. Which statement about it is most accurate?
choices: It serves as the seller's warranty that the home has no defects at all
It makes a professional home inspection unnecessary for the buyer
The listing broker should fill it out so that the answers are accurate
It reflects the seller's actual knowledge and doesn't replace an inspection
questions.explanation: The seller completes the disclosure from actual knowledge; the broker shouldn't fill it out. It isn't a warranty and isn't a substitute for an inspection.

questions.stem: A Colorado seller's home was the site of a suicide two years ago. Nothing about the home was physically damaged. Under Colorado law, this fact is
choices: a material fact the seller must disclose on the disclosure form
not a material fact that must be disclosed
a latent defect the listing broker must disclose in writing
required to be disclosed only if the buyer has young children
questions.explanation: C.R.S. 38-35.5-101 provides that facts or suspicions that a property was the site of a homicide, other felony or suicide are not material facts requiring disclosure, and a broker can't be sued for not disclosing them. Stigma isn't a physical defect.

questions.stem: A buyer notices that the neighbor's fence seems to sit several feet inside the lot line shown on the plat, and a shed appears to straddle the boundary. What should the buyer's broker recommend?
choices: A radon test before the inspection deadline passes
Relying on the seller's property disclosure statement
A survey to locate the boundaries and any encroachments
Having the broker measure the lot and report the result
questions.explanation: When boundaries, fences or encroachments are in question, a survey is the expert tool. Brokers should recommend experts rather than act as one.

questions.stem: A landlord is renting a house built in 1960 to a family on a one-year lease. Under the federal lead-based paint rule, which is required before the tenant is bound?
choices: Give the tenant a 10-day opportunity to conduct a lead inspection first
Give the EPA pamphlet and disclose any known lead-based paint
Remove all lead-based paint from the house before the lease begins
Nothing, because the lead-based paint rule applies only to sales
questions.explanation: For pre-1978 housing, landlords must give the pamphlet, disclose known lead-based paint and hazards, and include the warning statement. The 10-day inspection opportunity applies to buyers, not tenants, and the rule never requires removal.

questions.stem: A buyer's inspector finds mold on basement drywall next to a leaking water line. What is the essential first step in addressing the mold?
choices: Paint over the stains with a sealing primer
Install a radon mitigation fan in the basement
Wrap the affected drywall in plastic sheeting
Fix the leak to stop the moisture
questions.explanation: Mold grows wherever there's moisture, so fixing the water source is essential. Covering the mold without stopping the moisture just hides the problem.

questions.stem: Foam insulation blown into the walls of a home in the 1970s is suspected of releasing formaldehyde gas. This insulation is most likely
choices: friable asbestos
radon
UFFI
lead-based paint
questions.explanation: Urea-formaldehyde foam insulation (UFFI) was installed in the 1970s and can release formaldehyde gas. Radon is a soil gas, and asbestos releases fibers, not formaldehyde.

questions.stem: A buyer wants to fill a marshy part of a rural parcel to build a barn. The area is a federally protected wetland. What will the buyer typically need?
choices: A Phase I environmental site assessment report
Flood insurance through the NFIP before building
Approval from the seller's title insurance company
A permit from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers
questions.explanation: Wetlands are protected under the Clean Water Act, and filling or building in them typically requires an Army Corps of Engineers permit. A Phase I assessment relates to contamination and CERCLA defenses.

questions.stem: To hide a known roof leak, a seller paints over the ceiling stains and tells the buyer the roof has never leaked. Before closing, the buyer discovers the leak, wants out of the contract and wants the earnest money back. Which is most accurate?
choices: The buyer must close, because a stained ceiling is a patent defect
The contract is voidable by the buyer, who can seek rescission
The seller may keep the earnest money as liquidated damages
The contract is void, so neither party ever had obligations
questions.explanation: Concealing a known defect and lying about it is fraud, which makes the contract voidable by the victim. Rescission cancels the contract and returns deposits. The stains were hidden, so the defect wasn't patent.

questions.stem: A tenant with a lease option paid a separate option fee. Ten months into the lease, the tenant gives the owner written notice exercising the option. Which is true now?
choices: The option is still unilateral, so the tenant may decline to buy
The owner may refuse to sell if a higher offer comes in first
A bilateral purchase contract binds both the tenant and the owner
The arrangement converts into a right of first refusal
questions.explanation: An option is unilateral until exercised; once the optionee exercises it, it becomes a bilateral purchase contract binding both parties. The optionor can't back out for a better offer.

questions.stem: A buyer's offer on a home built in 1950 includes the Lead Warning Statement and lead disclosure as an attachment, signed along with the contract. This attachment is best described as
choices: an addendum
an amendment
a counteroffer
a contingency
questions.explanation: An addendum is material made part of the contract when it is signed; the federal rule requires the Lead Warning Statement in an attachment to the sales contract. An amendment changes a contract after it is formed.

questions.stem: A purchase contract with a time-is-of-the-essence clause includes an inspection contingency with a deadline. The inspection reveals serious defects, and the buyer gives written notice of termination before the deadline. Which result is most likely?
choices: The buyer is in default, and the seller keeps the earnest money
The seller can get specific performance forcing the buyer to close
The termination isn't effective until the seller signs an amendment
The buyer can terminate without being in default
questions.explanation: When a contingency fails and the buyer gives timely written notice, the buyer can terminate without default, so liquidated damages don't apply. Meeting the deadline matters because time is of the essence.
